newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: LAST YEAR A BAD ONE FOR RETAILERS, SAYS PEAK BODY
People are starting to spend their spare money on things other than shopping, according to the the National Council of Independent Retail Organisations.
Bureau of Statistics trend figures for November, released last week, show a decline nationally in retail turnover for the fifth month in a row.
The Council's Ian Baldock says the retail sector has been losing ground, as people spend their spare dollars on things such as eating out and gambling.
He says people in Queensland, gambling last year was worth 6.5 billion dollars, compared to retailing which was worth 21 billion dollars.
Mr Baldock says last year was the worst for retail traders in Australia since the recession.
BULLIMORE RESTING AFTER SURGERY
British yachtsman, Tony Bullimore, has been resting overnight in St John of God Hospital, in the Perth suburb of Subiaco, after undergoing exploratory surgery on his frostbitten fingers.
A hospital spokeswoman says the surgery appeared to have gone well, but this will be detailed in the surgeon's report, available later this morning.
Mr Bullimore fell into a deep sleep yesterday evening after he was given a sedative to calm him prior to surgery.
He'd been on the go all day after receiving a tumultuous welcome when he arrived in Fremantle aboard HMAS Adelaide with the other yachtsman rescued in the Southern Ocean, Frenchman, Thierry Dubois.
The hospital says more will be known about the medical outlook for the tough Briton after a bedside visit this morning from the doctor who performed last night's exploratory surgery.
SCG TRUST TO GET TOUGH ON DRUNKS
The Sydney Cricket Ground trust will have to ensure it's complying with its liquor licence at today's game....or face prosecution.
The Ground's been put on notice by State Gaming and Racing Minister Richard Face, who claims some aspects of the licence haven't been complied with.
Mr Face says bars should only be open for half an hour before the game, and for up to an hour afterwards, and shouldn't serve liquor in bottles or cans.
He says age restrictions must be enforced, and those intoxicated shouldn't be served.
The minister's also considering banning the sale of all BUT low alcohol beer.
Special inspectors will police liquor laws at today's match. - - - -
WATCH COMMITTEE WELCOMES QLD MOVE ON DEATHS IN custody

The Black Deaths in Custody Watch Committee says Queensland's decision to establish a group to examine the 1991 recommendations, of the black deaths in custody report, may prompt other states and territories to do the same.
The Indigenous Advisory Committe, to be chaired by former Senator Neville Bonner, will make recommendations to the Government based on the findings of the original black deaths report.
Watch Committee secretary, Cynthia Riley, says it's an important move, with three deaths in custody in the past two weeks in New South Wales.
She says the Queensland Government's move may assist in the original recommendations being implemented on a daily basis.
LES MURRAY WINS POETRY PRIZE
Australian poet Les Murray has won the 10-thousand dollar T-S Eliot prize for his latest collection -- Subhuman Redneck Poems.
One of the world's most prestigious poetry prizes, the award was announced at a ceremony at the British Library in London.
Educated at Sydney University, Murray was was born in the small town of Bunyah on the New South Wales mid-north coast, where he still spends most of his time writing.
He once wrote speeches for Prime Minister John Gorton.
